summary: P95/P99 latency spikes and request timeouts linked to continuous batching behavior
description: Issue summary: Multiple customers (starting with Acme Retail) reported p95/p99 latency spikes and intermittent request timeouts for text-generation endpoints. Spikes correlate with periods of low request concurrency and appear tied to the continuous batching component of the serving runtime. Impact: Customer-facing degradation for production workloads causing user-facing timeouts (5xx/504) and increased tail latency. Severity: Sev1 for affected customers on dedicated capacity. Environment: prod clusters in us-east with traffic mirrored to us-west; Dedicated pool ID: dp-acme-04. Observed behavior: sudden p95/p99 increases up to 2-3x baseline and occasional request timeouts during low-to-medium sustained QPS (~5-20 QPS per model). Expected behavior: continuous batching should maintain stable tail latency by batching short windows without introducing long head-of-line waits. Timing: First report 2026-02-20 09:08 UTC. Correlated SLO violations starting 2026-02-20 09:10-09:35 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a steady 5-20 QPS of short prompt requests (seq len ~64) to redwood-open-7b-v1 in prod/us-east
2) Observe latencies and streaming behavior over a 30 minute window
3) Compare p50/p95/p99 across two runs: continuous_batching enabled (default) vs continuous_batching disabled
4) Reproduce more readily by adding a burst protocol of 0.5-2s idle gaps between request groups to trigger batch flush heuristics
observed_logs: 2026-02-20T09:12:14Z serving-runtime: batch_scheduler: flush_delay exceeded for batch_id=0x1a9f, num_requests=3, calculated_wait=120ms
2026-02-20T09:12:14Z api-gateway: upstream timeout for request_id=req-83b2 (504), route=/v1/generate
2026-02-20T09:13:01Z serving-runtime: kv-cache hit ratio normal, no evictions
2026-02-20T09:13:03Z serving-runtime: CPU spike on host gpu-12 (cuda kernels queued), tail_latency 670ms (baseline 240ms)
initial_mitigation: 1) Scoped mitigation applied: pinned Acme Retail pool to batch_policy=aggressive-flush (reduces batching window) at 2026-02-20T10:05 UTC
2) Temporary rate-smoothing applied at edge (api-gateway) to reduce bursty arrivals and reduce long waiting batches
3) Recommended immediate customer-side workaround: set client to use concurrency=1 and enable client-side retry with exponential backoff
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Continuous batching adaptive heuristics over-estimate wait time in low concurrency traffic patterns causing head-of-line wait and increased p95/p99
Hypothesis B: Interaction between adaptive continuous batching and kernel selection causes uneven scheduling leading to queueing on certain GPU hosts
Correlated evidence: Instances showing flush_delay logs and 'calculated_wait=120ms' corresponded with tail latency spikes; when policy forced aggressive flush tail latency returned to baseline
Trace link: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/abcd-1234 (sample trace with 504 and batch flush event)
SRE reproduced locally by running a replica of the dedicated pool with traffic pattern 10 QPS with 0.5-1.5s gap between bursts; enabling continuous_batching reproduces p99 spike within 3-5 minutes
next_steps: 1) Engineering: Add logging to batch scheduler to capture decision metrics (estimated_wait, actual_wait, num_requests) for 24h across affected pools (ENG-assign: Carlos Ruiz)
2) Engineering: Create a canary config that changes adaptive thresholds (reduce max_wait_threshold from 200ms->50ms) and roll to a subset of dedicated pools (ENG-assign: Serving runtime team)
3) Product/Support: Notify affected customers of mitigation and ETA for permanent fix; offer temporary config toggle (continuous_batching=false) per-customer
4) Postmortem: If fix rolled, create postmortem and add regression test to CI to exercise low-concurrency batching behavior

Permanent fix pending canary results and follow-up PR.

Permanent fix path: adjust adaptive continuous-batching heuristics and improve kernel dispatch coordination to avoid head-of-line wait inflation
